title: FORGIVE MY SIN — JUST THIS ONCE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Pharaoh quickly summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you. Now forgive my sin once more and pray to the Lord your God to take this deadly plague away from me."" - Exodus 10:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Pharaoh says the right words again: I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you.

But look at the details, because they give him away. He says the Lord your God — not my God. He is still keeping his distance. And what he actually wants is stated plainly: take this deadly plague away from me. Not change me. Not receive me. Just remove the consequence.

There is also the phrase forgive my sin once more, which quietly admits this is a repeat performance. He knows the pattern and expects it to work again.

We should let this examine us gently rather than harshly. Have I ever confessed something to God chiefly to escape its consequences? Have I used God's forgiveness as a way to keep a habit comfortable?

David's prayer went in a different direction: create in me a pure heart, O God (Ps 51:10). He wanted a changed heart, not just a cleared record.

God does forgive genuinely repentant people, every time. But repentance that only wants relief has not yet reached the heart.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When I confess, am I asking for cleansing or just for relief?
2. Do I speak of God as "the Lord" or as "my Lord"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are my God, not just someone else's. Give me a repentance that goes deeper than wanting the consequences removed. Amen.
